title: The silent killer of analog reliability: Why SPICE misses floating net
gist: A Siemens EDA product engineer argues SPICE simulation systematically misses floating nets in analog power-down modes because of gmin stepping, time-scale limits and coverage gaps, contributing to re-spins. He promotes automated structural analysis with Calibre Insight Analyzer as a shift-left fix.

insights.claim: According to the Wilson Research Group / Siemens EDA Functional Verification Study, first-silicon success rates have hit a historic low, with nearly 68% of designs requiring two or more spins.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Re-spin rates raise cost and schedule risk that favours investment in verification tooling.
insights.locator: The semiconductor industry is currently facing

insights.claim: Analog and mixed-signal verification remains a primary source of re-spins even though digital verification has matured with formal methods and constrained-random testing.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: AMS verification is the weaker link, a growth area for EDA vendors.

insights.claim: As designs move to advanced nodes and aggressive power management, floating nets have grown from a niche concern to a critical reliability bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Power-gating adoption increases exposure to this class of defect.

insights.claim: A floating net is a node disconnected from all low-impedance paths to supply or ground in a power-down state, so its voltage is set by trapped charge on parasitic capacitances and drifts over time through leakage.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Explains why power-down modes create latent defects invisible in normal operation.
insights.locator: The anatomy of a floating net

insights.claim: If a floating node's drifting voltage reaches the threshold of a connected transistor it can turn that device on, causing unregulated power routing, latch-up or permanent damage to the device or downstream components.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: A small structural defect can cause field failures and costly re-spins.
insights.locator: Because no node is perfectly isolated

insights.claim: Designers cut bias currents and supplies to analog IP blocks such as LDOs, amplifiers or PLLs with MOSFET switches in power-down modes to extend battery life and manage thermal envelopes.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Shows why power-down structures are ubiquitous in low-power design.

insights.claim: SPICE simulators use gmin stepping, adding a very high-impedance resistor from every node to ground to avoid a singular matrix, which masks floating nets by providing a ground path that does not exist in silicon.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: The simulator's convergence aid hides the exact defect being sought.

insights.claim: Floating net failures are time-dependent, with nodes taking milliseconds or seconds to drift to critical voltage, and standard simulations rarely run that long because of computational cost.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Short simulation windows structurally cannot expose slow-drift defects.

insights.claim: Detecting floating nets requires covering every combination of power-down states and sequences, and in an SoC with dozens of power domains the permutations are astronomical, so transient simulation alone cannot cover them.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Exhaustive testbench coverage is infeasible, motivating structural methods.

insights.claim: In one analyzed design, a 'VICTIM' net feeding the gate of a large PMOS pass transistor was left floating in power-down; simulation masked it, but in silicon trapped charge partially turned on the transistor during a long idle period, causing a current spike that damaged the output stage.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Illustrates how a simulation-clean design failed in the field and required a re-spin.

insights.claim: Automated structural analysis such as Calibre Insight Analyzer finds defects from circuit topology rather than transient behavior, parsing the netlist and layout and evaluating connectivity against all defined power modes.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Positions Siemens' Calibre tool as the shift-left alternative to simulation.

insights.claim: The tool follows three steps: mode definition of power states, topological checking for nodes lacking a low-impedance path to supply or ground, and reporting with cross-probing to layout and schematic.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: A concrete workflow that engineers can adopt before signoff.

insights.claim: Typical fixes for flagged floating nets include adding a high-impedance bleeder resistor or a tie-off cell.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Remediation is cheap if the defect is found early.

insights.claim: With 3D IC architectures and heterogeneous integration, power delivery complexity will increase and the author says automated structural analysis is becoming a mandatory requirement for analog signoff.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Vendor-authored claim suggesting rising demand for reliability signoff tools.
